topic: abu sayed killing case verdict release
headline_marked: 809-page [[full verdict released in Abu Sayed killing case]]
headline: 809-page full verdict released in Abu Sayed killing case
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has published the comprehensive judgment involving 30 accused, including a former university VC.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has released the full 809-page verdict in the case regarding the killing of Abu Sayed during the July uprising.
The judgment involves 30 accused individuals, including Hasibur Rashid, the former Vice-Chancellor of Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur.
According to the tribunal, the full verdict contains extensive discussions on the evaluation of evidence, judicial analysis, and the fairness of the trial process.
The court noted that the killing of Abu Sayed was one of the most significant events in the first phase of the crimes against humanity committed during July and August.
The tribunal stated that the trial was conducted transparently, neutrally, and fairly, following international standards, and expressed hope that the verdict would establish justice.
The original sentence was announced on April 9 by a three-member judicial panel led by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury.
The sentencing included death penalties for two accused, life imprisonment for three, 10-year terms for five, 5-year terms for eight, and 3-year terms for 11 others.
One accused was considered to have served their sentence based on the time already spent in custody.
caption:
A massive 809-page verdict has been released detailing the killing of Abu Sayed.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has released the full 809-page verdict in the case regarding the killing of Abu Sayed during the July uprising.

The judgment involves 30 accused individuals, including Hasibur Rashid, the former Vice-Chancellor of Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur.

According to the tribunal, the full verdict contains extensive discussions on the evaluation of evidence, judicial analysis, and the fairness of the trial process.

The court noted that the killing of Abu Sayed was one of the most significant events in the first phase of the crimes against humanity committed during July and August.

The tribunal stated that the trial was conducted transparently, neutrally, and fairly, following international standards, and expressed hope that the verdict would establish justice.

The original sentence was announced on April 9 by a three-member judicial panel led by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury.

The sentencing included death penalties for two accused, life imprisonment for three, 10-year terms for five, 5-year terms for eight, and 3-year terms for 11 others.

One accused was considered to have served their sentence based on the time already spent in custody.
